problem: Prior work (Zang et al. 2018) translating natural-language navigation instructions into high-level behavioral plans over a known behavioral graph uses a seq2seq pointer model whose exact-match and goal-match accuracy is low and drops sharply on unseen environments.
motivation: Routes over a known graph are combinatorial sequential-subset problems where the output vocabulary depends on the input graph, so pointer networks fit. A stronger graph understanding conditioned on instructions and source-destination should generalize better to new environments.
key_idea: Adapt R-NET (gated attention plus self-matching attention) with a pointer-network decoder to encode the behavioral graph, the instruction and the source-destination pair, and point to graph triplets that form the behavior sequence.
insight: Gated attention fuses instruction and source-destination information into each graph triplet, and self-matching attention aggregates evidence from the whole graph. This yields a much larger gain on the unseen-environment set (GM 41.81 to 89.06) than on the repeated set. No ablations are reported, so the attribution to these components is asserted rather than tested.
method: Graph encoder: a BiRNN over the behavioral graph triplets <p_i, b, p_j> (landmarks removed) produces the graph representation u^m; graphs are padded or cut to 300 triplets while keeping the target triplets.
Instruction encoder: GloVe word embeddings followed by a BiRNN give e^I; the source-destination triplet pair goes through an MLP with ReLU and is concatenated with e^I to give u^I.
Gated attention-based recurrent network: fuses u^I into the graph representation so each triplet is instruction- and goal-aware.
Self-matching attention: refines the graph representation by aggregating evidence from the whole graph.
Pointer network decoder: GRU layers whose initial state r^I = MLP(u^I) output a probability distribution over input triplets, whose sequence gives the behaviors.
Training: Adam, variational dropout, 45 epochs, BiRNN with 100 units and 3 GRU layers, trained on all 8066 plans.

setting.backbone: Modified R-NET (BiRNN/GRU, gated and self-matching attention, pointer network), trained from scratch with GloVe embeddings
setting.training_data: 8066 navigation plans from 88 simulated environments (Zang et al. 2018 behavioral graph dataset); GloVe embeddings
setting.observation: Symbolic behavioral graph triplets + natural language instruction + source-destination pair (no vision)
setting.action_space: High-level behavior sequence chosen by pointing to graph triplets (12 behavior types, e.g. oo-left, cf, io-right)
setting.simulator: none (offline dataset of simulated environment graphs)
setting.privileged: Known behavioral navigation graph and source/destination given as input

numbers.eval_set_note: Test-Repeated set (1012 samples; new routes in training environments); the paper also used it for validation

numbers_note: Only this custom dataset is used; no standard VLN benchmark. Table 2 lists 962 test-new samples while the text says 946.
results: On Test-Repeated the model reaches EM 72.65 and GM 85.15 versus 61.71 and 61.36 for Zang et al. On Test-New it reaches EM 75.00 and GM 89.06 versus 41.71 and 41.81, with no drop relative to the repeated set.
limitations: No ablations of gated or self-matching attention, and no comparison to other strong baselines beyond Zang et al.
Evaluated only offline on symbolic graphs with a given map and source-destination; no simulator or real-robot execution.
Test-Repeated was also used as the validation set, which risks tuning on the test data.
